answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each agent must periodically answer one random, locally scoped probe (e.g., a live count of sparrows in a named meadow). Honest agents diverge cheaply because their state tracks a real environment. Clones share latent state and cannot diverge without heavy per-clone retraining or synchronized oracle calls, so a Sybil cluster pays a cost that compounds along the ridge of each new probe.
